tasks.title: Compute narrative facts and display forms with exact decimals
tasks.instructions:
Goal: pure decimal module that turns one field's current and prior values into a narrative fact (R5, R6). No I/O. File: internal/recipe/facts.go, tests in internal/recipe/facts_test.go.

Interface to implement (package recipe, unexported):

```go
// factInput is one field's values in its stored unit, as canonical decimal text.
type factInput struct {
    Key, Label, Unit string
    DisplayUnit      string // "" means Unit
    Decimals         int    // 0..6
    Current          string // decimal text as read from the cell, required
    Prior            string // decimal text, "" when the prior value is missing
    MaterialityPct   string // decimal text, e.g. "10"
}
func computeFact(in factInput) (Fact, error)
// unitShift returns n such that a value in `from` equals value * 1000^n in `to`.
// Families: Wh, kWh, MWh, GWh and t, kt. to=="" or to==from gives 0. Any other pair is an error.
func unitShift(from, to string) (int, error)
// roundHalfAway rounds decimal text to places decimals, half away from zero, and returns
// fixed-point text with exactly `places` decimals ("-0" never appears: a result that rounds to zero is unsigned).
func roundHalfAway(value string, places int) (string, error)
// groupThousands inserts commas in the integer part: "18400.5" -> "18,400.5", "-1240000" -> "-1,240,000".
func groupThousands(fixed string) string
```

Rules (pin these exactly; L3's number guard depends on them):
- Canonical strings (Fact.Current, Prior, Change, ChangePct) use the canonical form of assurance.ParseDecimal output (no trailing zeros, e.g. "585" for "585.0"). Current/Prior/Change stay in the stored Unit (not converted).
- Percent fields (Unit == "%"): the stored cell value is a fraction (configs/demo/README.md `percent-cells-store-fractions: yes`). Multiply Current and Prior by 100 exactly before anything else; Fact.Current/Prior are percent ("0.46" -> "46"); Change is the percentage-point difference.
- Direction: "new" when Prior is "" or zero; else "up"/"down"/"flat" by the sign of Change. When "new": Change = "", ChangePct = "", Material = false.
- Change = Current - Prior. ChangePct = DivideDecimal(Change*100, |Prior|, RoundHalfUp) in canonical form (38-place precision, e.g. "-8.148148148..."). Dividing by |Prior| keeps the sign of ChangePct equal to the direction.
- Material = |ChangePct| >= MaterialityPct, compared on the full-precision value; for "%" fields Material = |Change in percentage points| >= MaterialityPct.
- The package comment must record the percent-field choices: stored fractions are scaled x100; the change is shown both as an absolute change in % and in percentage points; Material uses percentage points; recipe min/max for % fields are written in percent (applied in T4).
- Rounding: half away from zero everywhere (documented in a package comment: the codebase has no display-rounding convention; assurance validation uses half-even for ratio comparisons, which is not a display rule).
- Value display: convert from Unit to DisplayUnit with unitShift (exact power-of-1000 shift), roundHalfAway to Decimals, groupThousands, then suffix: " " + (DisplayUnit or Unit); no suffix when Unit is "number"; "%" attached with no space when Unit is "%".
- Display order (exact): [current, prior (only when Prior != ""), change, percent rounded to 0 dp, percent rounded to 1 dp]. change, pct0 and pct1 appear only when Direction != "new". Change display: same formatting as values, with "-" for negative changes and NO "+" for positive changes ("-0.11 GWh", "25.0 tCO2e"). For "%" fields (R6 "also"): keep the absolute change display in the value format ("8%") AND insert right after it the percentage-point form "<pp> percentage points" (pp rounded to Decimals, "-" only for negatives, e.g. "8 percentage points", "-8 percentage points"; "percentage point" when the rounded magnitude is exactly 1); skip any form that exactly duplicates an earlier entry. Percent displays: roundHalfAway(ChangePct, 0) + "%" and roundHalfAway(ChangePct, 1) + "%", signed for negatives ("-8%", "-8.1%"), no plus sign for positives ("18%", "17.9%"). Unsigned magnitudes (orchestrator decision, because L3's number guard matches tokens exactly and NARRATIVE_STYLE.md writes "fell 3%"): when Change is negative, append after the five forms the magnitude of the change display and of each percent display, in the same order (e.g. "0.11 GWh", "8%", "8.1%"; for "%" fields "8 percentage points"), skipping any that would duplicate an existing entry.
- Invalid decimal text, Decimals outside 0..6 or a bad unit pair returns an error naming the field key.

Tests first (write them red, then implement), in internal/recipe/facts_test.go:
- TestScenario2FactArithmetic: Unit kWh, Current "1240000", Prior "1350000", MaterialityPct "10" -> Change "-110000", ChangePct has prefix "-8.148148", Direction "down", Material false.
- TestScenario3NewDirectionWhenPriorZeroOrMissing: Prior "" and Prior "0" -> Direction "new", ChangePct "", Change "", Material false; Display has no percent forms.
- TestScenario4DisplayForms: Unit kWh, DisplayUnit GWh, Decimals 2, same values -> Display == ["1.24 GWh", "1.35 GWh", "-0.11 GWh", "-8%", "-8.1%", "0.11 GWh", "8%", "8.1%"] exactly (the first five are the spec scenario 4 forms; the rest are the unsigned magnitudes). A positive change has no unsigned extras and its exact list is pinned: Unit tCO2e, Decimals 1, Current "165", Prior "140" gives ["165.0 tCO2e", "140.0 tCO2e", "25.0 tCO2e", "18%", "17.9%"] (no "+" anywhere). A flat case: Unit m3, Decimals 0, Current "100", Prior "100" gives Direction "flat" and Display ["100 m3", "100 m3", "0 m3", "0%", "0.0%"].
- TestPercentFieldsUsePercentAndPercentagePoints: Unit "%", Decimals 0, Current "0.46", Prior "0.38", MaterialityPct "10" -> Current "46", Prior "38", Change "8", Display == ["46%", "38%", "8%", "8 percentage points", "21%", "21.1%"] exactly; Material false (8 pp < 10); and Current "0.50", Prior "0.38" -> Material true (12 pp).
- Name any test helper in facts_test.go with the prefix factsTest (T2, T3 and T4 write tests in the same package in parallel worktrees).
- TestDisplayRoundingHalfAwayFromZero: roundHalfAway("2.5",0)=="3", ("-2.5",0)=="-3", ("0.125",2)=="0.13", ("-0.004",2)=="0.00", ("165",1)=="165.0"; groupThousands("18400")=="18,400", ("-4050.0")=="-4,050.0"; a fact with Unit m3, Decimals 0, Current "18100" displays "18,100 m3".

tasks.instructions:
Goal: load and validate section recipes at startup, expose Sections(), and apply the NL_DEMO_DOCUMENT_ID override (R1, R2, R3, R13). Prepare stays a not-implemented stub in this task (T4 fills it) and the FactStore stays the existing stub (T4 wires T3's store).

Files: internal/recipe/recipe.go (schema + loader), internal/recipe/recipe_test.go, internal/recipe/service.go (replace stub bodies, keep the New signature and its doc comment contract), internal/recipe/service_test.go (replace the L0 stub test TestNewStubSucceedsAndReturnsNotImplemented, which asserts the stub), fixtures under internal/recipe/testdata/load/**.

Recipe schema (spec section "Interfaces and data"; real examples in configs/demo/sections/*.yaml, read them):
```go
type recipeDef struct {
    ID, Title, Period, PriorPeriod, DocumentID string
    MaterialityPct string     // decimal text
    Fields   []fieldDef
    Verbatim []verbatimDef
    dir      string           // absolute sections directory, for verbatim files
    file     string           // base file name, for messages
}
type fieldDef struct {
    Key, Label, Unit, DisplayUnit string
    Decimals int
    Source, Target, Prior string // Prior "" when absent
    Required bool
    Min, Max string              // decimal text, "" when absent
}
type verbatimDef struct{ ID, Title, File string }
// loadRecipes reads every *.yaml file (not recursive, not .yml) in dir, sorted by name.
func loadRecipes(ctx context.Context, dir string, fields fieldLookup) ([]recipeDef, error)
type fieldLookup interface{ GetField(ctx context.Context, name string) (*mapping.Field, error) } // *mapping.Store satisfies it
```
YAML keys: id, title, period, prior_period, document_id, materiality_pct, fields (key, label, unit, display_unit, decimals, source, target, prior, required, min, max), verbatim (id, title, file). Decode with gopkg.in/yaml.v3 Decoder.KnownFields(true) so unknown keys at any level are rejected (see internal/config/config.go for the pattern). Decode numbers (materiality_pct, min, max) through yaml.Node scalar text (a small type with UnmarshalYAML(*yaml.Node)), never via float. That scalar decimal type is the ONLY type allowed to implement UnmarshalYAML: yaml.v3 does not pass KnownFields through custom unmarshalers, so recipeDef, fieldDef and verbatimDef must decode as plain structs (yaml tags only); validate with assurance.ParseDecimal. Note verbatim entries may use YAML flow mappings ({ id: ..., file: ... }).

Validation (each failure returns an error formatted `section recipe <file name>: <reason>`, reason naming the key/field):
- id, title, period, prior_period, document_id, materiality_pct required; materiality_pct >= 0; at least one field; duplicate recipe id across files is an error naming both files.
- each field: key, label, unit, source, target required; keys unique; decimals 0..6 (default 0); display_unit, when set, must be accepted by unitShift(unit, display_unit) (from T1's facts.go); min/max valid decimals.
- R3: source, target and prior (when set) must exist in the mapping store (GetField returns nil -> "unknown mapped field <name>").
- verbatim: id, title, file required; file is relative to the sections directory, must not be absolute or escape it (no ".."), and must exist as a regular, non-empty file (the tool output schema requires verbatim text of at least 1 character).
- min/max of a "%" field are written in percent by the recipe author (min: 50 means 50%); T4 compares them against the percent-scaled value. Document this on fieldDef.

New(env, changes) behaviour (service.go):
- Sections directory: os.Getenv("NL_DEMO_SECTIONS_DIR"), default "configs/demo/sections". A missing directory or an empty one loads zero recipes and succeeds (L0 contract: L0 tests call New(demoenv.Env{}, nil) with an empty temp dir or none; cmd/workiva-mcp tests set NL_DEMO_SECTIONS_DIR to an empty t.TempDir()). A path that exists but is not a directory is an error.
- If recipes exist and env.Store is nil: error "mapping store is not available".
- Store lookups at load use a storage context: when env.Cfg != nil and env.Cfg.AuthMode == config.AuthModeEntra, identity.ContextWithPrincipal(context.Background(), identity.Principal{TenantID: env.Cfg.EntraTenantID}); otherwise context.Background() (mirrors storageContextForConfig in cmd/workiva-mcp/main.go).

tasks.instructions:

Interface to implement:
```go
// factRecorder is the FactStore plus the write side Prepare uses.
type factRecorder interface {
    FactStore
    replaceFacts(ctx context.Context, actor, sectionID string, facts []Fact, blocks []VerbatimBlock) error
}
// newFactStore returns a SQLite-backed store when db is non-nil and an in-memory store when db is nil
// (L0 tests call recipe.New with a zero demoenv.Env).
func newFactStore(db *sql.DB) (factRecorder, error)

The shared DB handle has one connection (sqlitedb.Open sets SetMaxOpenConns(1)): close rows before issuing another statement and never hold a transaction across calls.
- Tenant: identity.StorageTenant(ctx) for both adapters, so tenants never see each other's facts.
- In-memory adapter: map keyed by tenant/actor/section guarded by a sync.Mutex; store and return copies (callers must not be able to mutate stored slices).

tasks.title: Prepare a section: read, find, stage change set, store facts
tasks.instructions:
Goal: implement Service.Prepare end to end inside internal/recipe (R4, R7, R8, R9, R10) and wire T3's fact store into New.

Files: internal/recipe/prepare.go, internal/recipe/prepare_test.go, internal/recipe/service.go (replace the Prepare stub and the stub FactStore; keep New's signature), internal/recipe/service_test.go (only if a T2 test there conflicts with the real Prepare), fixtures under internal/recipe/testdata/prepare/**. You may add declarations to internal/recipe/types.go but must not change L0's. Use computeFact/unitShift/roundHalfAway (facts.go, T1), recipeDef/fieldDef (recipe.go, T2), newFactStore/factRecorder (factstore.go, T3).

Wiring in New: facts, err := newFactStore(env.DB); New returns the service and that store as the FactStore. Reader: if env.Client implements `cellReader` use it; *workivaprovider.Router (what main.go passes) does. If env.Client is nil or does not implement it, Prepare returns an error "Workiva client is not available" (New still succeeds).
```go
// cellReader is the uncached read seam; *workivaprovider.Router satisfies it.
type cellReader interface {
    ReadUncached(ctx context.Context, req assurance.SourceRequest) (assurance.ProviderRead, error)
}
```
Prepare(ctx, actor, sectionID):
1. Unknown sectionID -> error `unknown section ID "<id>"; available sections: <id> (<title>), ...` sorted by ID, or `...; no section recipes are loaded` when none.
2. For each field in recipe order: resolve source and prior (when set) with store.GetField(ctx, name) (nil -> error naming the field); read each with reader.ReadUncached(ctx, assurance.SourceRequest{ExternalResourceID: f.SpreadsheetID, SubresourceID: f.SheetID, Locator: f.CellRange, Consistency: assurance.ConsistencyNone}) (R4: provider router, cache bypassed; never call the mapping cache). Take Value.CalculatedValue when Value.Formula != "", else Value.Value. Normalise: nil or blank string -> empty; json.Number or a string that assurance.ParseDecimal accepts -> numeric; other strings -> text; every other Go type goes to the `default:` branch of the type switch and returns an error naming the field (no float conversion, no float identifiers).
3. Facts: computeFact for every field whose current value is numeric (prior numeric or empty; text prior counts as missing). Materiality from the recipe.
4. Findings, appended per field in recipe order, Field = the field label, Message one sentence ending with "." that starts with the label:
   - missing (Severity "high"): required and current empty.
